transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (CTO - Northbound), Elena Ortiz (Platform Eng), Priya Kaur (SRE)

Summary:
Short readout of week 3 bench results vs incumbent provider, routing/playbook decisions for canary, and handoff to provisioning for a dedicated slot if they move forward. Discussed a few outlier latency spikes tied to tail QPS, and one KV-cache warmup issue. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Throughput and p50/p95/p99 latency deltas vs baseline
- Outlier investigation (cold KV cache, burst QPS)
- Routing policy for mixed traffic and fallback model variants
- Security handoff: KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps for dedicated slot provisioning and pilot close criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda—lucas will run the perf highlights and then we'll talk routing and next steps.
[00:18] Samir (Northbound): sounds good. we ran the nightly load at 1.2k rps overnight, got the traces over, thx.
[00:32] Lucas (Redwood SE): ok i'll share my screen in a sec, i'm going to pull up the trimmed csv. top-line: compared to your incumbent we see a 22% lower per-token compute cost and p50 latency is roughly the same, p95 down by about 18%, p99 overall improved but note the 3 spike windows around 03:14:xx.
[00:58] Elena: those spike windows—are those correlated with a particular request pattern? we had a few large batches from the feed ingestion.
[01:10] Lucas: partially. looking at the traces, two of the three spikes line up to a KV cache miss during a prefix-heavy workload, and one aligns with a sudden mini-burst where concurrent context length increased.
[01:29] Priya: the KV cache miss—does that mean warmup or eviction?
[01:34] Lucas: it appears to be warmup after a platform rotation; the tenancy we used for that run rolled nodes and the in-memory prefix K/V had to refill. in prod we'd mitigate with pre-warm or sticky routing.
[01:50] Maya: important note—our routing configs can pin warm users to a sticky slot while others go through autoscale, to avoid that warmup tail.
[02:03] Samir: can you quantify the tail impact? like 99.9 or 999? we saw a few customer-visible latencies above 800ms.
[02:12] Lucas: p99.9 spike windows reached ~920ms in those events; outside of spikes our p99 is ~380ms, incumbent was ~460ms under similar conditions.
[02:24] Elena: ok that's helpful. i also noticed CPU steal on the orchestration host for one sample, might be noisy neighbor noise from our k8s cluster.
[02:36] Maya: worth calling out—this POC used Redwood hosted staging; if you move to dedicated, that noisy neighbor noise disappears and you get predictable throughput.
[02:48] Samir: we're still evaluating cost vs latency; the committed slot cost is a chunk but predictable.
[02:55] Maya: yes, that's expected. we'll put together a few committed sizing options in the pricing sheet.
[03:06] Lucas: another point—our quantize profile for this model reduced token cost by ~28% with minimal quality delta on your test prompts. we did a quick ngram-based QA check, didn't see regression but full eval would be needed.
[03:24] Priya: did you run the quantized path under the same batcher and kernel set? i'm worried the quant path behaves differently under long contexts.
[03:34] Lucas: we did two runs: one with default continuous batching and the quant path had slightly higher memory ops but lower kernel time; for context>1024 we observed slightly higher variance but still better median. that's why for canary we suggested routing short-context traffic to quantized variant.
[03:57] Samir: right the bulk of our traffic is short, but about 12% of requests exceed 1500 tokens.
[04:06] Maya: suggested routing policy: 1) short (<1024) -> quantized variant, 2) mid -> baseline fast model, 3) long -> full fp16 model. plus fallback to incumbent if latency thresholds breach.
[04:20] Elena: does Redwood support dynamic fallback per-request? or is it per route?
[04:26] Lucas: we can do per-request routing based on headers and observed SLOs; there's also automatic fallback rules where if error or latency breaching occurs, traffic will shift to a compatible variant or to the baseline provider as last resort.
[04:40] Samir: oh so you can set SLO of like 500ms p99 and then have automatic fallback?
[04:45] Lucas: correct, you express a policy and the smart router enforces with circuit-breaker style thresholds.
[04:52] Priya: in the spike where KV warmed up, how quickly did the system recover?
[04:56] Lucas: the warmup cost about 12–18s to refill KV for that slot; with sticky routing you'd avoid evicting the warm slot so your tail would be much smaller.
[05:09] Maya: note: we also saw a couple of malformed trace entries where transcript tagging misattributed the model name — minor transcription issue—sorry i mean the profiler had one label as "Redwood Dedication" which is wrong.
[05:22] Samir: ha, okay.
[05:25] Elena: security question—when we move to dedicated, how are keys handled for inference? we need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs for tokens.
[05:35] Maya: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments; for Redwood Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS and full audit logs accessible in the console. we'll share the SOC2 artifact as well.
[05:48] Samir: we need CSV of the audit log format so our compliance team can validate ingestion.
[05:55] Maya: noted, action item.
[05:58] Lucas: back to perf—throughput: you had a 48% higher sustained concurrency threshold on Redwood for the chosen instance type, mostly due to our continuous batching and kernel selection. that translated to about 1.6x throughput at iso-latency compared to incumbent in the mid-range load test.
[06:19] Priya: is that mostly at token-level batching or request-level?
[06:22] Lucas: token-level continuous batching plus dynamic packing of short sequences. so short request packing improved average GPU utilization.
[06:30] Samir: any caveats around streaming vs non-streaming paths? we stream partial results to clients.
[06:36] Lucas: streaming has a slight overhead—it increases client-side visible latency for first bytes by ~10–20ms in our runs, but overall tail is similar; if you rely on early partials it's fine.
[06:47] Elena: we ran a special mis-specified header once and it routed to the fallback model; logging showed a 502 then automatic failover, which is good.
[06:56] Maya: that's the fallback playbook working.
[06:58] Samir: ok, so where are we on pilot success criteria? we set goal of p99 < 500ms for 80% traffic and unit cost <= incumbent.
[07:08] Lucas: right now p99 for 80% of traffic is ~420ms on Redwood (after excluding the KV warm windows). unit token cost is ~14% lower than incumbent in our runs.
[07:20] Priya: i want to make sure our long-tail users are not impacted—we can't have critical flows above 900ms.
[07:26] Lucas: understood; plan for canary: route 5% traffic to Redwood with sticky routing for a sample user cohort that includes long-context flows so we can validate tail under realistic mix.
[07:40] Samir: i like that. what about canary observability? we need tracing link instrumentation and SLO alerts.
[07:47] Maya: console provides per-route latency and token-level cost, and you can plug tracing headers into your existing Jaeger/Zipkin. we'll provide a sample instrumentation snippet.
[07:58] Elena: also need per-tenant cost breakdown and per-token cost attribution for our finance team.
[08:04] Maya: yep we'll include that in the pricing packet and show how to pull token-level CSVs from the API.
[08:11] Samir: security again—SSO/SAML mapping for roles? we want RBAC for engineers vs ops.
[08:18] Lucas: supported, you can map SAML groups to RBAC roles in the private control plane.
[08:23] Priya: any gotchas for VPC egress? we need strict allowing of subnets and IP ranges.
[08:29] Maya: for dedicated we can provide customer-dedicated NATs and fixed egress IPs; for private/on-prem we'll mirror your network rules.
[08:38] Samir: perfect. all right let's talk logistics—if we decide to proceed with a dedicated slot what's the earliest start?
[08:46] Maya: provisioning lead time is typically 7–10 business days after contract and sizing finalization; for express case we can fast-track to 3 days with a small setup fee.
[08:56] Elena: ok, and the pricing options you mentioned—can you give a ballpark now?
[09:01] Maya: roughband: small committed pool for your baseline QPS would start at $XXk/mo, midsize at $YYk/mo, enterprise slots with DR at $ZZk/mo. i'll send exact numbers in the pricing sheet.
[09:12] Samir: got it.
[09:14] Lucas: one more technical caveat—the benchmarking harness we used had a slightly different tokenization for a corner prompt, which caused a 2-token discrepancy in one test. doesn't materially change the unit-cost math but wanted to flag it.
[09:27] Priya: that's fine as long as you annotate it in the CSV.
[09:31] Lucas: noted.
[09:35] Maya: ok let's recap to be clear — next steps: redwood will upload trimmed CSVs, pricing, canary routing suggestion; northbound sends prod traces and confirms compliance artifacts needed; schedule provisioning call week of 6/21 if go-ahead.
[09:49] Samir: yep, and can we have a short EC2 style cost breakdown by token and by request?
[09:55] Maya: yes we'll include token and request-level breakdown in the CSV and a one-pager.
[10:00] Elena: also email me the audit log schema.
[10:03] Maya: will do.
[10:06] Priya: any reason we should rerun the overnight load with sticky routing enabled before canary?
[10:11] Lucas: good catch—yes we can run one more targeted test with sticky routing enabled to show the tail improvement; we suggest that before the canary starts.
[10:20] Samir: agreed, schedule it.
[10:24] Maya: action items recorded. anything else?
[10:28] Elena: no, that's it. thanks.
[10:31] Samir: thanks everyone.
[10:33] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few speaker mislabels and a couple misspellings (e.g., "Redwood Dedication" instead of "Redwood Dedicated") and tokenization note captured.

Attachments referenced: pricing-sheet-draft.xlsx (link sent after call), trimmed-benchmarks-2026-06-10.csv (to be uploaded), security-soc2-summary.pdf (to be shared).
